text:
This looks like mid-2008: fed funds near 2%, headline CPI at 5.5% (peak was 5.6% in July 2008), and unemployment at 5.7%. Unemployment was 5.7% in July 2008 and 6.1% in August, so July or August is plausible.

Headline CPI of 5.52% fits June 2008 (5.0%) or July 2008 (5.6%). The actual figures are June 5.02%, July 5.60%, August 5.37%, so 5.52 is roughly July. Unemployment of 5.7% with a 3m change of +0.7 would be consistent with a series that was 5.0% in April, which doesn't match. The unemployment series may be a different vintage.

Gold fell 9.3% in the month, which fits July 2008 (gold went from about 930 to 913 and then fell further in August to about 830). A 3m equity return of -6.8% is also more consistent with August than with July. The 2-year yield at 2.37% fits August (about 2.3%), and the 10-year at 3.79% fits August (about 3.8%). US large-cap equity returned +1.5% in the month, which matches August 2008 (S&P +1.2%). EM equity at -6.3% fits August too.

So the snapshot is most likely August 2008.
